title: Compact probe experiments for KV warmth and TTL tuning
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick lab notebook for a small set of probe experiments to measure and tune KV cache TTL and prefetch behavior across tenants. Aim is to produce observable signals we can use to: (1) reduce cold-token tail latency, (2) avoid eviction storms that harm tenant fairness, and (3) produce compact dashboard surfaces for oncall.

Background / why this is different:
- We have a lot of instrumentation already, but most dashboards are high-cardinality and noisy.
- Eviction behaviour (esp. during bursts) seems to correlate with tail latency and cost spikes. Need a small, repeatable probe harness that can: vary TTL/prefetch budgets, tag probes by tenant class, and sample traces with KV attr annotations.
- Prior art: earlier kv-warmth signals and warm-start probes exist but are heavy-weight. This is intentionally compact and experiment-focused.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Increasing TTL by x% for mid-frequency tenants reduces 95th TTFB by ~10% without significantly increasing GPU memory churn.
- H2: Small staged prefetch (budgeted to 10ms per request) increases kv_prefetch_hit_rate and reduces downstream decode latency for multi-turn chats.
- H3: Eviction storms are often caused by synchronized cold-starts from a small group of high-volume tenants; attenuating probe cadence reduces cross-tenant impact.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Variant A: baseline TTL (current prod) + no prefetch (control)
- Variant B: TTL * 1.5 for a cohort of 10 low-medium tenants (randomized)
- Variant C: TTL * 1.5 + prefetch budget 10ms (per-request background prefetch)
- Variant D: TTL * 0.8 + probe attenuation (lower cadence) for a cohort of high-volume tenants (test fairness)
- Duration: 72h per variant, ramped to capacity-simulated load in staging then small canary in prod (5% traffic)

Key metrics to collect (defns, how to compute):
- kv_warmth_ratio: fraction of requests that observe a KV cache hit for the requested prefix length. (hits / total_checks)
- kv_prefetch_hit_rate: fraction of subsequent token generations that used data populated by a prefetch within window W (W = 5s).
- ttl_distribution_p95: p95 of TTL values observed for evicted entries (use histogram aggregation).
- eviction_rate_per_min: number of evictions per minute per host (or per-GPU pool).
- tenant_eviction_bias_index: normalized ratio comparing eviction_rate_per_min for tenant cohort vs global median ( >1 indicates bias).
- ttfb_p95_tokens: time to first token p95 for requests that experienced cold vs warm cache. Label by span.attr.kv_hit.
- downstream_decode_latency_p95: p95 of generation loop after cache check pass/fail.
- probe_cost_per_hour: synthetic probe token cost tracked separately for cost accounting.

Alert/SLI suggestions (rough):
- SLO: ttfb_p95 for production <= 200ms for warm requests (kv_hit=true), <= 500ms for cold requests.
- Alert: eviction_rate_per_min per-host > 2x baseline for > 10m -> P1 investigation.
- Warning: tenant_eviction_bias_index > 1.3 for > 30m -> page oncall with tenant context.

Tracing plan (sampling + attributes):
- Sampling: deterministic sample every Nth request for probes (N configurable), plus biased sampling for trace-level debugging when eviction anomalies detected. Keep core production sampling unchanged.
- Span names:
  - span.kv.cache_check (start when checking cache)
  - span.kv.prefetch (background prefetch work)
  - span.kv.evict (eviction work)
  - span.kv.apply (apply fetched tokens into decode)
- Span attrs (key list):
  - kv.hit: true|false
  - kv.entry_ttl_ms: integer
  - kv.entry_size_bytes: integer
  - kv.prefetch_budget_ms: integer
  - request.seq_len: integer
  - request.model_variant: string (e.g., 'quantized-v2')
  - tenant.id (hashed)
  - probe.id (for our synthetic probes)
  - probe.variant (A,B,C,D)
- Trace-context: ensure we propagate probe.id through model fanout, routing, and into downstream operator spans so we can stitch end-to-end.

Dashboard panels (compact set, operator-focused):
- Panel 1: KV Warmth heatmap by tenant cohort (rows = tenant cohort buckets, cols = hour-of-day) with color = kv_warmth_ratio. Click -> tenant drilldown.
- Panel 2: Eviction rate timeline (hosts stacked) + p95 TTL overlay.
- Panel 3: TTFB p95 split by kv.hit (warm vs cold) and probe.variant (A..D).
- Panel 4: Prefetch efficacy: kv_prefetch_hit_rate over time and correlation scatterplot with downstream_decode_latency_p95.
- Panel 5: Tenant fairness indicator sparkline (tenant_eviction_bias_index for top-100 tenants).
- Panel 6: Probe harness health: probe_cost_per_hour, probe_success_rate, last_probe_timestamp.

Dashboard UX notes:
- Keep to 6 panels per microdash to avoid query cost blowup. Use pre-computed rollups for p95 and heat histograms.
- Add a small "what to check" cell with quick links: trace filter for probe.id, Jira test run id, and last config used.

Instrumentation sketch (practical):
- Add a lightweight probe runner in telemetry sandbox service (language: Go) that issues requests via the internal SDK with a probe header.
- Probes should be signed and annotated so routing/quotas exclude them from tenant billing.
- On cache miss, instrumentation emits a metric kv_cache_check{hit=0, tenant_hash, variant}. On prefetch, emit kv_prefetch_attempt and kv_prefetch_populated. Use low-cardinality tags: tenant_bucket (small set), host_pool.

Data storage / rollups:
- Short-term rollups (1m) for operational dashboards, 1h/1d for trends. Use Sketch summaries for p95 to save cardinality.
- Trace retention: keep probe traces at high fidelity for 14 days; aggregated trace anchors for 90 days.

Runbook snippets (investigation steps):
1) If eviction_rate_per_min spikes: check recent TTL changes (config audit), look at host mem pressure, open traces with span.kv.evict.
2) If tenant_eviction_bias_index > threshold: drill into tenant cohort heatmap, check traffic patterns and large prefix fanouts.
3) If kv_prefetch_hit_rate is low despite attempts: inspect prefetch budget attr and server-side queueing for prefetch worker.

Open tasks / TODOs:
- [ ] Create probe harness PR and config flip flags (owner: Maya) -> GitHub PR linked above.
- [ ] Define tenant buckets mapping (low/med/high) and hash function (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Dashboard wireframe mock (owner: Harpreet), include drilldown template.
- [ ] Small staging run (72h) and analyze results; schedule postmortem.
- [ ] Add entitlement filter so probes don't affect quota metering.

Risks and mitigation:
- Probe noise could change scheduling behaviour: run in staging first and cap probe rate.
- Added trace attrs increase cardinality: restrict tenant.id to hashed bucket and only propagate full tenant id on investigator opt-in.

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep probe.id prefix with date + short uid so we can grep traces quickly.
- We might want to try a randomized TTL jitter instead of fixed multiplier to see if jitter reduces synchronized evictions.
- Consider coupling probe cadence with synthetic user journeys (multi-turn) to better simulate KV reuse.

Post-experiment success criteria (quick):
- Reduce cold-request ttfb_p95 by >= 8% for target cohorts without >5% increase in eviction_rate_per_min or memory churn.
- Produce dashboard templates that SREs can use during rollouts with <4 queries per panel.

Appendix (quick refs):
- Example query snippets: (pseudo)
  - pctile(95, ttfb_ms) by kv.hit, probe.variant over 1m
  - count(eviction) by host, tenant_bucket over 5m
- Related tickets: JIRA-OBS-981 (experiment plan), JIRA-OPS-1203 (alert tuning)
notes: Informal lab doc. Expect to iterate on metrics names and panel queries during the first staging run.
